ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic sentence أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I am a pupil (girl).
   B. I am a pupil (boy).
   C. My name is Ahmad.
   D. I am well, thanks be to God.

2. A girl asks another girl maa ismuki? What is she asking? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the book?
   B. How are you?
   C. What is your name?
   D. Who is this?

3. What does the Arabic sentence أَبِي يَعْمَلُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is my mother.
   B. My father works.
   C. This is my father.
   D. I have a brother and a sister.

4. Which Arabic room word is made from the words ghurfa and nawm? (1 mark)
   A. the kitchen
   B. the garden
   C. the bathroom
   D. the bedroom

5. What does the Arabic word مَدْرَسَةٌ (madrasa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. yesterday
   B. day
   C. Monday
   D. school

6. Which is a rule of good turn taking? (1 mark)
   A. Interrupt without saying anything
   B. Wait until the speaker has finished
   C. Speak at the same time as others
   D. Shout to be heard

7. What does the Arabic word لَا (laa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. song
   B. your turn
   C. cake
   D. no

8. What does the Arabic sentence عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيدٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Happy birthday.
   B. Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   C. May you be well every year.
   D. Blessed festival (Happy Eid).

9. What does the Arabic word لَحْمٌ (lahm) mean? (1 mark)
   A. meat
   B. eggs
   C. carrots
   D. bread

10. Which sentence means 'Do you like bananas?' (1 mark)
   A. aakulu l-mawz
   B. hal tuhibbu l-mawz?
   C. uhibbu l-mawz
   D. ashrabu l-mawz

11. What does the Arabic sentence هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I drink water.
   B. I eat bread.
   C. Do you like bananas?
   D. I like bananas.

12. Which Arabic sentence means "I write with my hand." (1 mark)
   A. أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   B. أَكْتُبُ بِيَدِي
   C. أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي
   D. أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي

13. What does the Arabic sentence أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I smell with my nose.
   B. I speak with my mouth.
   C. I see with my eye.
   D. I hear with my ear.

14. What can help a nervous speaker? (1 mark)
   A. Practising many times before speaking
   B. Speaking very quickly
   C. Whispering
   D. Not preparing at all

15. Which is good body language for a speaker? (1 mark)
   A. Looking at the floor
   B. Standing straight and looking at the audience
   C. Turning your back
   D. Hiding behind the paper

16. How do you read the syllable جَ? (1 mark)
   A. nu
   B. ja
   C. li
   D. muu

17. How is the Arabic word عَمَّةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ʿamma
   B. ibn
   C. ukht
   D. ab

18. In a passage about the home, which of these is a theme word? (1 mark)
   A. shukran
   B. al-ahad
   C. marhaban
   D. kursii (chair)

19. What does the Arabic sentence الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   B. On the table there is a cup.
   C. How are you? (to a girl)
   D. The house is big.

20. How is the Arabic word الْجُمُعَةُ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. al-yawm
   B. al-ithnayn
   C. al-jumuʿa
   D. usbuuʿ

21. What does the Arabic sentence أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I read a book on Sunday.
   B. I visit my grandmother on Friday.
   C. I help my mother on Saturday.
   D. I drink water.

22. What is a good aim in a reading contest? (1 mark)
   A. To read without looking
   B. To read as loudly as possible
   C. To read correctly and smoothly
   D. To read as fast as possible

23. What is a prediction? (1 mark)
   A. A spelling test
   B. A list of words
   C. A copy of a picture
   D. A sensible guess about what will happen next

24. How is the Arabic word نَعَمْ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. naʿam
   B. hafla
   C. baaluun
   D. mabruuk

25. What does the word mufiid mean? (1 mark)
   A. big
   B. useful
   C. delicious
   D. cold

26. What does the Arabic question mark ؟ tell the reader? (1 mark)
   A. Read very fast
   B. The voice rises at the end
   C. Stop reading
   D. The voice falls

27. What does the Arabic sentence لِي عَيْنَانِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My body is strong.
   B. This is my body.
   C. I have two hands.
   D. I have two eyes.

28. What does al-miftaahu fii l-khizaana mean? (1 mark)
   A. The chair is at the door.
   B. The key is in the cupboard.
   C. The lamp is above the table.
   D. The pen is in the bag.

29. What does the Arabic word كُوبٌ (kuub) mean? (1 mark)
   A. knife
   B. cat
   C. cupboard
   D. cup

30. How is the Arabic word بَابٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. taawila
   B. kitaab
   C. saaʿa
   D. baab

31. What is the difference between ح (Haa) and خ (khaa)? (1 mark)
   A. khaa has a dot below
   B. khaa has a dot above and Haa has none
   C. Haa has a dot above and khaa has none
   D. They are the same letter

32. What is the name of the Arabic letter ب? (1 mark)
   A. dhaal
   B. Haa
   C. baa
   D. siin

33. Which sound does the Arabic letter ف make? (1 mark)
   A. th as in think
   B. f as in fan
   C. m as in mat
   D. t as in tap

34. Which of these is a characteristic of good handwriting? (1 mark)
   A. Even spacing between words
   B. Different sizes of letters
   C. Large gaps inside a word
   D. Smudges

35. Which Arabic sentence means "The chair is new." (1 mark)
   A. الطَّاوِلَةُ صَغِيرَةٌ
   B. الْبَابُ كَبِيرٌ
   C. النَّافِذَةُ نَظِيفَةٌ
   D. الْكُرْسِيُّ جَدِيدٌ

36. Which sentence means 'The window is clean'? (1 mark)
   A. at-taawilatu Sagiira
   B. al-kursiyyu jadiid
   C. al-baabu kabiir
   D. an-naafidhatu nadhiifa

37. What does the Arabic word الثُّلَاثَاءُ (ath-thulaathaa') mean? (1 mark)
   A. Monday
   B. Thursday
   C. Tuesday
   D. Wednesday

38. What does the Arabic sentence هَذَا مَطَرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The wind is strong.
   B. This is the sun.
   C. This is rain.
   D. The sun is hot.

39. What does al-jawwu mumtir mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is sunny.
   B. The weather is rainy.
   C. The weather is cloudy.
   D. The weather is cold.

40. Which is the correct order for the sentence 'The pen is in the bag'? (1 mark)
   A. al-qalamu fii l-haqiiba
   B. fii l-haqiiba
   C. fii l-qalamu l-haqiiba
   D. l-haqiiba al-qalamu fii

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Translate into English: abii yaʿmalu (2 marks)

42. Translate into English: jaddatii tuhibbunii (2 marks)

43. Rearrange the words to make a sentence and translate it: الْخَمِيسِ / يَوْمُ / الْيَوْمُ. (3 marks) (3 marks)

44. Translate into English: adhhabu ilaa l-madrasa yawma l-ithnayn (2 marks)

45. Explain how a family celebration you know helps people to live together in peace. (3 marks) (3 marks)

46. Translate into English: al-kitaabu ʿalaa t-taawila (2 marks)

47. Translate into English: ar-riihu qawiyya (2 marks)

48. Give three rules for taking turns in a conversation. (3 marks) (3 marks)

49. Translate into English: alʿabu yawma s-sabt (2 marks)

50. Give three points you would check when you assess a friend's reading. (3 marks) (3 marks)

51. Explain why vocabulary building helps you to learn Arabic. (3 marks) (3 marks)

52. Translate into English: haadhihi ummii (2 marks)

53. Translate into English: anaa ʿinda l-baab (2 marks)

54. Put these words in order and translate: الْحَفْلَةَ / أُحِبُّ / أَنَا. (3 marks) (3 marks)

55. Translate into English: ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub (2 marks)

56. Translate into English: man haadhaa? (2 marks)

57. Translate into English: fii l-usbuuʿi sabʿatu ayyaam (2 marks)

58. Write five household items in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

59. Give three tips for neat handwriting with good word spacing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

60. Write the Arabic sounds and meanings of four position words. (4 marks) (4 marks)

61. Write four foods or drinks in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

62. Translate into English: ʿiid mubaarak (2 marks)

63. Translate into English: uhibbu baytii (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — I am well, thanks be to God.
   أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (anaa bi-khayr, al-hamdu lillaah) means: I am well, thanks be to God.

2. C — What is your name?
   maa ismuki? asks a girl for her name. The ending -ki is used for a girl.

3. B — My father works.
   أَبِي يَعْمَلُ (abii yaʿmalu) means: My father works.

4. D — the bedroom
   ghurfatu n-nawm means 'the room of sleep', which is the bedroom.

5. D — school
   مَدْرَسَةٌ (madrasa) means school.

6. B — Wait until the speaker has finished
   Good speakers wait for their turn and use polite words if they must interrupt.

7. D — no
   لَا (laa) means no.

8. A — Happy birthday.
   عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيدٌ (ʿiid miilaad saʿiid) means: Happy birthday.

9. A — meat
   لَحْمٌ (lahm) means meat.

10. B — hal tuhibbu l-mawz?
   hal makes a question and tuhibbu means 'you like'.

11. C — Do you like bananas?
   هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ؟ (hal tuhibbu l-mawz?) means: Do you like bananas?

12. B — أَكْتُبُ بِيَدِي
   أَكْتُبُ بِيَدِي (aktubu bi-yadii) means: I write with my hand.

13. D — I hear with my ear.
   أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي (asmaʿu bi-udhunii) means: I hear with my ear.

14. A — Practising many times before speaking
   Practice makes a speaker calm and confident.

15. B — Standing straight and looking at the audience
   Eye contact and a steady stance help the audience to listen.

16. B — ja
   جَ is read ja.

17. A — ʿamma
   عَمَّةٌ is read ʿamma and means father's sister.

18. D — kursii (chair)
   A theme word belongs to the topic. A chair is found in the home.

19. D — The house is big.
   الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ (al-baytu kabiir) means: The house is big.

20. C — al-jumuʿa
   الْجُمُعَةُ is read al-jumuʿa and means Friday.

21. B — I visit my grandmother on Friday.
   أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ (azuuru jaddatii yawma l-jumuʿa) means: I visit my grandmother on Friday.

22. C — To read correctly and smoothly
   Accuracy and smoothness matter more than speed.

23. D — A sensible guess about what will happen next
   We use clues to predict what may happen next.

24. A — naʿam
   نَعَمْ is read naʿam and means yes.

25. B — useful
   mufiid means useful or good for you.

26. B — The voice rises at the end
   A question ends with a rising voice.

27. D — I have two eyes.
   لِي عَيْنَانِ (lii ʿaynaani) means: I have two eyes.

28. B — The key is in the cupboard.
   miftaah is key and khizaana is cupboard.

29. D — cup
   كُوبٌ (kuub) means cup.

30. D — baab
   بَابٌ is read baab and means door.

31. B — khaa has a dot above and Haa has none
   khaa is Haa with one dot above.

32. C — baa
   The letter ب is called baa.

33. B — f as in fan
   The letter ف makes the sound f as in fan.

34. A — Even spacing between words
   Good handwriting has even spacing, correct shapes and neat presentation.

35. D — الْكُرْسِيُّ جَدِيدٌ
   الْكُرْسِيُّ جَدِيدٌ (al-kursiyyu jadiid) means: The chair is new.

36. D — an-naafidhatu nadhiifa
   naafidha is window and nadhiifa is the feminine form of clean.

37. C — Tuesday
   الثُّلَاثَاءُ (ath-thulaathaa') means Tuesday.

38. C — This is rain.
   هَذَا مَطَرٌ (haadhaa matar) means: This is rain.

39. B — The weather is rainy.
   mumtir means rainy.

40. A — al-qalamu fii l-haqiiba
   The item comes first, then the position word and the place.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: My father works.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: My grandmother loves me.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ الْخَمِيسِ. Today is Thursday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first word, 1 mark for the correct order and 1 mark for the translation.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: I go to school on Monday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: People meet, share food and joy, sing and talk together, and learn to respect one another.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meeting, 1 mark for sharing, 1 mark for respect.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The book is on the table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: The wind is strong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen until the speaker finishes; do not speak at the same time; use polite words to interrupt; give others a chance.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid rule.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: I play on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Words pronounced correctly; smooth reading without stops; heavy and throat sounds clear; no word skipped.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: The more words you know, the more you can understand, say and write. Grouping words by theme helps you to remember them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for understanding, 1 mark for speaking or writing and 1 mark for remembering.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my mother.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am at the door.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْحَفْلَةَ. I like the party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first word, 1 mark for the correct order and 1 mark for the translation.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: On the table there is a cup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who is this? (a boy or man)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: There are seven days in a week.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example bayt (house), ghurfa (room), matbakh (kitchen), hammaam (bathroom), hadiiqa (garden).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Leave a gap about one letter wide between words; keep letters in a word joined smoothly; write on the baseline; put dots neatly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid tip.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: fii (in), ʿalaa (on), taHta (under), fawqa (above).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

61. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example khubz (bread), aruzz (rice), maa' (water), haliib (milk).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: Blessed festival (Happy Eid).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

63. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like my house.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.
